title: Swap a fresh cake in under a pastry display dome and cover it
instruction: Put the cake where the empty plate is, under the dome, and cover it with the dome. Don't touch the cake.
context: Counter staff in cafes and bakeries swap cakes under display domes many times a shift. The dome hangs and sways from its small knob, the plates have to trade places on the display spot, and the dome has to come down square around the cake.
setup: One fixed layout on the station table (top 0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y to the left). Display spot: x 0.30 m, y 0.10 m. Empty plate: flat glazed ceramic, 250 mm across, 12 mm thick, 0.60 kg, loose, centred on the display spot. Pastry display dome, clear polycarbonate (American Metalcraft LFTD8 size), 206 mm across and 168 mm tall overall: a 20 mm straight skirt, a rounded top on a 103 mm radius, a 30 mm neck 8 mm tall and a 40 mm ball knob; 2.5 mm wall, 0.43 kg; resting rim-down on the empty plate, centred over the spot. Cake plate: the same kind of plate, centred at x 0.30 m, y -0.19 m (a 40 mm gap between the plates' edges). Sponge cake, 152 mm across, 60 mm tall, 0.50 kg, on the cake plate's centre. Nothing else.
scoring: 0 for the whole trial once the cake has been knocked (moved 3 mm or tilted 3 degrees relative to its plate; moving or tipping the plate with the cake on it does not count). How the plates and the dome are moved is up to the robot. Otherwise from the final state: 0.25 if the cake's plate is centred within 15 mm of the display spot; 0.5 if also the dome covers the cake (its rim lower than the cake's top, the whole cake inside its wall and under its top, dome tilted under 10 degrees); 1.0 if also the dome's rim rests wholly on the cake's plate (within 2 mm of the plate's top, the dome's centre within 20 mm of the plate's, tilt under 2 degrees). Every positive score needs both hands' fingertips and pad midpoints at least 80 mm from the dome, both plates and the cake, and all four still for the last 1 s (no two positions of a tracked point 1 mm apart).
reset_notes: Put the empty plate back on the display spot with the dome on it, and the cake plate with the cake at its start.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only. The dome's rounded top is drawn as five rings of flat panels (within 1.3 mm of the sphere) and the knob as stacked discs, in the simulator's glass material, which renders tinted; knob sizes are scaled from the product photo and the mass from the wall's area. The cake is a rigid cylinder, so a touch shows as the cake moving or tilting rather than as a dent in its icing.
